question: Does the frozen learned controller improve VOD visual quality or playback outcomes over the highest-allowed rule under the same safety filter?

scope.training: none; use frozen checkpoints for diagnostic screen

policies.name: highest_allowed
policies.selection: highest representation permitted by the checkpoint safety filter

baselines.name: bola_basic
baselines.implementation: BOLA-Basic score using log bitrate utility and observation-v2 nominal candidate sizes; no explicit wait action

baselines.name: bola_basic_filtered
baselines.implementation: Same BOLA-Basic score, with the frozen checkpoint safety mask

quality_metric.name: VMAF
quality_metric.alignment: decoded output frames aligned at 25 fps; upscale each distorted rung to source resolution with bicubic scaling before VMAF so resolution loss remains measured

known_limits: The four transfer sessions are from one historical ferry route.
The source network traces were collected in 2010-2011.
Only two source videos are available; Sintel is the held-out content.
BOLA-Basic uses nominal candidate sizes and approximates its no-download decision with the highest-scoring rung; the simulator buffer cap supplies the wait at full buffer.
BOLA-FINITE startup/wind-down adaptation and its explicit pause action are not implemented in this first baseline screen.
BOLA gamma_p=5 is the published example parameter, not tuned for this project.
Metric tool is installed locally; record its exact version and build configuration in the output manifest.
VMAF results are quality diagnostics for these generated encodes and do not establish human acceptance.
selection_rule: No model or policy selection from these test cases; report all cases and retain failures.
